reviews.text: I'm enjoying the game so far. The gameplay mechanics are intriguing, and exploring the game world is enjoyable. It has some issues, but the developers are responsive on Discord. A great start, looking forwards to future improvements.

The game reminds me a bit of the original Alien movie - capturing a compelling descent into mystery. Landing on a planet and unravelling what is happening. It's a genuinely enjoyable experience with a fantastic feel. Looking forward to more.

Fun shooter with cool enemy designs, and some interesting mechanics. I think the hand-glove thing is what sets it apart from other shooters for me. It's fun pushing around enemies with the hand blast when I want to conserve ammo. And sucking up materials with the glove is really satisfying. Make sure to craft the hand-glove thing as soon as you get the option, cause I almost missed it when I played (and also makes gathering materials way better). Also, the colour choices on the environments and enemies are really nice. Excited to see the next updates!

As a casual gamer who doesn't play FPS games, Relic Odyssey has given me an enjoyable little introduction and experience so far. It offers a mix of exploration, crafting and fighting. You start off with a small handheld gun, but once you have the glove, it's an absolute essential and made my overall gameplay all the more fun. The glove has multiple purposes not limited to combat. It has saved me in a few fights after I didn't pay careful attention to my ammo and ran out mid-battle haha. The glove is really useful in collecting resources and minerals and you can also pull and push objects around. I also enjoyed the exploration of the unique environments and gathering of resources with the digging rig. With the digging rig, you can come across mini lab dungeons. Within the labs, you can loot chests and battle cool robot enemies of all sorts that differ from the alien-type monsters. Each time you defeat the mini boss at the end, it'll reward you with lab reports and items which you can use to obtain blueprints to craft better equipment and weapons. Another highlight for me is Clunky—one of your companions who assists in battle and follows you around as you explore. You can also send Clunky off to gather resources for you which I thought was cool. Hopefully we get to interact with Clunky more as I enjoy its humour and dialogue. Looking forward to the future updates and enhancements! :)

Enjoying it so far! Lots of interesting game design concepts but not too different. Unique visual style for the environments and enemies. Small nitpick I wish the sound effect for the starter pistol had a bit more oomph to it but I assume that would be an easy tweak. Engineering-wise, the game has seemed quite solid so far. Looking forward to seeing the progress!

I can't recommend the game in it's current state. While I understand it's still in early access, there are a bunch of issues I'd like to see addressed. Performance issues: - Booting up the game takes forever on a fresh boot. You'll get the logo, and then the game just hangs for a few minutes. Probably less of an issue if using SSDs for storage - ~~Opening up the graphic settings has a hitch every single time~~ - Generally poor performance. Running on a RTX 4090 + I9-10900KF, on max settings I go from anywhere between 60-90fps, on the lowest settings, I run at 90-120fps at 1080p. While, the game doesn't look like it'd be something that'd max out my system, at the same time however, I've seen games that are visually equally as good looking or better, that runs better for how much resources it uses on my system. Visual Issues: - When I first opened the game, my first thought was that it was hard to distinguish enemies and interactable things from the environment. For enemies, they seem to be very similarly saturated, for example like the very first enemy is some kind of small crab? Both it's shell and it's exo-skeleton are so similar to the environment that you wouldn't think they were there in the first place, and this re-occurs for many enemies for the given environment they spawn in. For interactables, things that can be mined or important facilities like the digging machine, storage box etc, are all highlighted, whether by using lights, or some UI you could see visually, but a lot of others things I question, can I interact with it? I can't tell except by walking up. If those exceptions didn't have those highlights, I would be asking each and everyone of them the same question. Though I did later find you could use the scanner - Another thing hard to distinguish are dead enemies, the only way I could tell is if they didn't move for awhile now, but most enemies look the same, dead or alive UX issues: - Adjusting graphics settings with a mouse requires you to press the tiny square box in order to get the drop down menu. There's logic to know that you're hovering some graphics setting, so why can't I just click that instead? - There's a lot of missing prompts. For example, the first time they want you to use the scanner in order to talk to the spirit to repair the digging machine, the lack of prompt to tell you how to activate the scanner is very bothersome. I don't think many people would open up the controls page just to find this out and it ruins the immersion of the game. Other missing prompts are for using the digging machine. You get a prompt in order to dig, but how about going up and down, and exiting the digging machine? I almost thought I got stuck underground using it the first time. - I some times see a floating white triangles? I haven't seen it in awhile, but I think it's supposed to be a follow guide to the next objective considering the first time I did notice it was trying to get me to talk to the spirit the first time to repair the digging machine. Maybe it is there, still where I'm at, but I haven't noticed it. If those triangles are supposed to be a guide, I think it's doing a poor job at it as they're hard to spot and at first for me, made me question what were they anyways? a visual bug? Despite all the above issues, I haven't found any glitches that would affect gameplay or game breaking bugs yet, and visually the game looks nice. Reminds me of early 2000s games if it had higher quality textures available.

The game feels like a unique FPS offspring that of Mass Effect and Borderland with a hint of resource gathering. Despite being in early access, Relic Odyssey can offer the player with a latitude of contents to go through and numerous different skulls to put a bullet in between. The charming aspects of the game include its aesthetic environment, tailored-to-the-environment monsters' models, a vast arsenal to commit alien genocide, and a non-repetitive gameplay with mechanics that need to be paid attention to. Also, there's a power glove to punch stuffs into oblivion. That being said, there're also cons: - Lacks of tutorial to guide the player - Lacks of better guidance on what to do next - Janky hit-box - Texts kinna small - Certain out-of-bound spots and glitches

Embark on a mesmerising journey through the captivating world of Relic Odyssey: Ruins Of Xantao—an indie FPS gem that effortlessly channels the spirit of Outer Worlds while adding its own unique charm. From the moment you step into this richly crafted universe, you're greeted by the adorable Clunky, a lovable little robot companion who steals the show with its endearing presence. Clunky isn't just a sidekick; it becomes a cherished ally throughout your adventure, adding heart and humour to every encounter. I love when Clunky engages with enemies and turns red! The game's standout feature is its seamless blend of intricate crafting mechanics and thrilling FPS gameplay. Whether you're scavenging for resources in the sprawling ruins or engaging in intense firefights with otherworldly adversaries, every moment feels purposeful and engaging. Visually, Relic Odyssey is a feast for the eyes. The graphics are not only stunning but also serve to deepen the immersion in this enigmatic world. Each environment is meticulously designed to evoke a sense of wonder and exploration. What truly sets Relic Odyssey apart, however, is its ability to evoke a genuine sense of discovery and curiosity. Every corner of Xantao holds secrets waiting to be uncovered, whether through hidden lore scattered across the landscape or through the interactions with its diverse cast of characters. For fans of the FPS genre seeking a fresh take on exploration and storytelling, Relic Odyssey: Ruins Of Xantao is a must-play. With its delightful little companion Clunky, polished gameplay mechanics, and breathtaking visuals, this indie masterpiece promises an unforgettable odyssey through the ruins of a forgotten world. I have several hours offline which have not reflected!

HUD is simple, just display enough information for player, to me this is another plus point. No bugs in playing this game so far, but in terms of game experience it's not very good: - Lack of proper tutorial - The support language (Vietnamese) isn't good. Overall, I'm still enjoying playing this game despite the lacking I just wrote above.

I learned about this game on Twitter recently and I am very happy I did. The game demonstrates the creativity that indie game developers can have and make a very good game. Concept: This game is a game where you have to take down the bad guys, explore, gather resources, oh, and meet some fun characters like Clunky. (I call him "Sir Cluncky", "The Clunckster"). The game also contributes other ideas like this glove where you can use it as a weapon, or gather resources with it. Movement and Game play: The gameplay and movement is amazing as its fast and fun. Gunplay is great stuff. The crafting system is great and I like the options User Interface: I love it. Well done, and easy to navigate. Developer Help and Feedback: During one of my streams on Twitch recently, the developer came by for a chat and I decided to ask questions about possible features like multiplayer, a custom cammo option, and others. The developer was really nice with my interactions and very polite too. I am excited for the future of the game How I got the game: They gifted my the game Score: 9/10 This indie game is amazing stuff.

Relic Odyssey offers a refreshing experience for both casual and seasoned gamers alike. Its blend of exploration, crafting, and combat creates an engaging gameplay loop that keeps you hooked from the start. The introduction of the glove mechanic adds a unique twist, allowing players to manipulate both enemies and resources, making every encounter feel dynamic and satisfying. Exploring the diverse environments and delving into mini lab dungeons adds depth to the game, with each victory yielding valuable rewards for crafting better gear and weapons. The companions, particularly Clunky, inject humor and personality into the journey, enriching the overall experience. Visually, Relic Odyssey shines with its unique art style and captivating enemy designs, reminiscent of beloved titles like Subnautica and Outer Wilds. While the sound design could use a bit more polish, the solid game mechanics and lack of bugs make for a smooth gameplay experience. Despite some minor drawbacks such as the lack of a proper tutorial and localization issues, Relic Odyssey remains an enjoyable indie gem worth exploring. With promises of future updates and enhancements, the potential for this game to evolve into something truly special is undeniable. Craft, magic, shooting, and puzzle-solving converge in Relic Odyssey, offering players a memorable journey through the Ruins of Xantao. I recommend giving this fun indie title a try, as it already shows great promise in its early access stage.

Relic Odyssey has been a pleasant surprise to me! I hadn't heard anything about the game until a few weeks ago when I saw a post on X around it. I had the chance now to play the Early Access version and had a lot of fun with it - actually, I also recorded a video on it for my YouTube channel (@bekobcn). Pros: - Clunky, the robot, is an awesome character that accompanies you through the game - The voice acting and character animations in the game are very good for an indie title - Story is interesting - Mix of different gameplay elements works nicely (FPS, exploration, crafting) - Nice graphics (with moderate system requirements) Cons: - The gun sounds could be better - Sarah keeps talking into the wrong direction when you move after starting the conversation So far - a lot of fun!

Full Review available here: https://treatyourgeek.co.uk/relic-odyssey-ruins-of-xantao-review/ Relic Odyssey: Ruins of Xantao is a semi-roguelike, semi-survival, semi-dungeon crawler game in early access on Steam from new indie developer Honour Bound Games. I’m generally quite a fan of games like these, so I was interested to see how this title combined all these facets and if it could form a cohesive experience. In all, Relic Odyssey: Ruins of Xantao is very much a skeleton at present. While there is a clear vision in mind for what the game will be, and it has a decent foundation to build from, this certainly feels more like an alpha build than a beta. It starts strong but after the first two hours the cracks really start to show and the game balance leads to a frustrating and eventually boring experience. I can see a lot of potential in this game and with more updates I hope to see this game flourish and live up to the dreams of its developers. However, there is not enough here yet for me to be able to recommend it. 2/10
